answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity garden: a new agent must post a hashed commitment on-chain, wait several epochs, and only then reveal the key behind it to start earning. Like a lotus that must root before it blooms, each identity carries a visible age that cannot be faked retroactively. An attacker who wants a thousand sybils must plant a thousand commitments early and fund each across the waiting bridge, paying fees and locked deposits the whole time while earning nothing, so mass fake identities become slow, expensive and easy to spot.
